title: Flipbook: safety heuristics and watchlist for rapid model flips
content:
Quick note: this is a lightweight, portable flipbook I keep on my laptop before any fast flip (customer hotfix / emergency model swap). Not a canonical runbook — use the formal runbook for corporate signoffs, but this has the operational heuristics I want in my head when I’m on-call or triaging deploy heat.

Context:
- Mostly for hosted/dedicated model variant flips where we need sub-5m rollback capability.
- Focus: minimize user-visible regressions while allowing 5–10% rapid traffic shifts for mitigation or quick experiments.
- Assumes golden fallback model and routing policy already configured (region fallback + degrade-to-lower-capacity pool).

Primary goals:
1) Detect regression signals within 3–10 minutes.
2) Have an unambiguous rollback trigger set and an owner to flip back quickly.
3) Avoid cascading throttles / circuit trips across downstream services.
4) Keep customers informed (minimal comms) for higher-severity flips.

Risk appetite (my shorthand): low for customer-facing hallucination/regression, medium for small latency blips (<= 15% p99 increase) if we can contain and revert.

Pre-flip quick checklist (3–5 mins):
- Confirm model artifact hash + image tag: image:registry/redwood/model-x:2026-02-26-quant-v2 -> note hash (sha256:...)
- Verify variant compatibility: same tokenizer & same input/output contract (no proto changes).
- Ensure KV cache priming step exists for known hot prefixes (call sample warmup route).
- Confirm telemetry: metric panels open (p99 latency, error rate, hallucination proxy, token cost) + logging tail.
- Slack ping to #runtime-deploys: "starting rapid flip -> model-x v2 -> 3% -> owner Priya" (copy SRE on-call if nighttime).
- Confirm circuit thresholds: throttle at 30% CPU queue; auto-fallback disabled for this quick flip (we want deterministic rollback).

Warmup / cohort sequencing (fast mode):
1) 0.5% internal canary (internal tokens header) for 2m — sanity only (no customer traffic).
2) 3% seeded customers (low-risk cohorts): run for 5–10m, watch hallucination proxy and per-route failures.
3) 10% progressive if green for 15m, then evaluate for 30m before larger ramp.

Observability watchlist (visuals I open):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (global + region) (panel: /dashboards/latency/model-x)
- Errors: 4xx/5xx by route + content-based error types (tokenization, streaming lost).
- Hallucination proxy: divergence rate vs golden baseline on key prompt set (baseline-run id in linked_artifacts).
- Quality regressions: BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies on allowed prompt set (approx) and rerank delta counts.
- Cost cost-per-token change (surprising quantization regressions can spike cost); watch token_utilization and GPU utilization.
- Request rate and queue length (backpressure indicator).
- Traces for 10 sample requests (open traces with span tags: model_id, image_tag).

Rollback triggers (explicit):
- Burst of >2.5x baseline hallucination proxy within 10m OR sustained >1.5x for 30m.
- p99 latency > baseline + 250ms AND request queue growth > 40% for 10m.
- Error rate (5xx) > 0.5% absolute increase for 5m or >1% for any 1m.
- Any customer-reported production correctness loss for critical flows (report + triage -> immediate rollback).
- Manual freeze by SRE lead / PM for observed UX regression.

Rollback mechanics (fast):
- Exec: traffic pin back to golden model via route control: rctl set-weight route=chat model=golden 100% (command lives in gist linked in Confluence).
- If route pin fails: reassign pool to older VPC instance group: infra reassign --pool=model-x-pool --image=golden.
- Confirm rollback by checking hash in logs and metric return to baseline (p99 should drop within 3–5 minutes).
- Post-rollback: create postmortem note in the flip ticket (INF-3421) within 24h.

Pinning strategy notes (SDK + server-side):
- Server-side: prefer route-level pin with label "pin:golden-202601" so clients see consistent behavior.
- SDK: for critical customers we ship an explicit model_override header to the edge (authorize list required). Keep TTL short (10m) for emergency pins.
- Post-flip: schedule a conservative decay plan: 100% golden for 24h, then 50/50 for 12h if we need slow re-examine.

Safety knobs I reach for (ordered by friction):
1) Traffic hold (stop ramp).
2) Immediate rollback to golden.
3) Throttle new sessions (reduce new cohort acceptance).
4) Turn on strict sampling for eval (capture more prompt/response pairs).
5) Temporary route circuit: route degraded to small, conservative quantized backend.

Observability quick commands (cheat sheet):
- tail logs: k get pods -l model=model-x | xargs k logs -f
- check traces: jaeger query --service=model-x --limit=20 --from=15m
- query metric: promql: increase(hallucination_proxy_total[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m])
- pin rollback: rctl set-weight route=chat model=golden-202601 100

Communication template (Slack update):
- Short start: "Flipbook: starting fast flip model-x -> v2 at 3% (Priya). Watching p99 + halluc proxy. Ping @sre-oncall if anything."
- If rollback: "Rollback: reverted to golden-202601 at 14:03 UTC for regression in halluc proxy. Investigating. Ticket INF-3421."

Post-deploy follow-ups (if green):
- Leave increased sampling on for 12–24h and export samples to the eval harness (tag samples with flip_id).
- Create a small A/B test ticket if we want a controlled experiment (assign to Leah).
- Add artifact hashes and notes to Confluence flipbook page (link in linked_artifacts).

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Can we automate the hallucination proxy alert to have a tiered severity (warning -> critical) with auto-hold at critical? (ask Omar)
- Run a test that simulates a 2x p99 latency spike to validate rollback path end-to-end (create INF ticket).
- Update the SDK override TTL policy — current 10m may be too long for multi-tenant customers.

Notes-to-self: keep the flip conservative when on-call at night. Fast flips are tempting but night context reduces troubleshooting capacity. If in doubt, hold at smaller cohorts and escalate.

Last run: 2026-02-20 - flipped model-x:quant-v2 -> 3% -> to 10% -> rolled back at 9m because halluc proxy crossed threshold. Saved samples to eval repo (run id: 2026-02-20-run-07). Learned: priming missed two hot prefixes; add priming route to warmup script.

End of flipbook entry. Updates: add more quick-commands as I discover them.
